description: What each adapter answers for the shared editor fixtures (cases.json), in the normal form of fixtures.cjs. "both" is the answer of both adapters. Where they differ today, "vscode" and "lsp" hold each answer and "difference" says why. t-40 removes the differences that are not adapter policy, one feature at a time. README.md says how to update this file.

hover: a code embed path.difference: Same text, different spacing. VS Code builds the hover with MarkdownString.appendCodeblock, which adds a blank line before the code block and a line break after it, and always fences with three backticks. The language server writes the fence itself and makes it longer than any backtick run in the code (lspAssist.ts embedHover).

completion: a front matter key on an emp.difference: VS Code adds the extension's contributed snippets (snippets/smd.json), shown as the one entry "(contributed snippets)". With no word at the cursor it offers all of them. The language server has no snippets. The keys from the providers are the same.

completion: an inline directive.difference: VS Code adds the contributed "Callout" snippet, whose prefix is ":::", shown as "(contributed snippets)". The language server has no snippets. The directives from the providers are the same.

completion: a container name.difference: VS Code adds the contributed "Callout" snippet, whose prefix is ":::", shown as "(contributed snippets)". The language server has no snippets. The container names from the providers are the same.

outline: the plan.difference: VS Code's outline shows headings only (language.ts SymbolProvider). The language server also lists requirements, acceptance criteria, decisions and risks under their headings (lsp.ts outlineSymbols) (CL-23).

lsp: EF-STORE — Prices are stored in cents [Interface] 9
outline: the store.difference: VS Code's outline shows headings only (language.ts SymbolProvider). The language server also lists the requirement under its heading (lsp.ts outlineSymbols) (CL-23).

references: a block id where it is given.difference: VS Code searches .smd, .md and .markdown files for references (language.ts workspaceDocuments), the language server .smd files only (workspace.ts collect), so the link in notes.md is found by VS Code alone (CL-23).

references: a link to a heading.difference: Two differences. VS Code searches .smd, .md and .markdown files for references (language.ts workspaceDocuments), the language server .smd files only (workspace.ts collect), so the link in notes.md is found by VS Code alone (CL-23). And asked on a link, VS Code resolves the link to the heading and lists the heading as the declaration (language.ts anchorAt). The language server lists a heading as the declaration only when the cursor is on the heading itself (lsp.ts references), so plan.smd line 10 is missing.

references: a :ref to a block in another.difference: VS Code searches .smd, .md and .markdown files for references (language.ts workspaceDocuments), the language server .smd files only (workspace.ts collect), so the link in notes.md is found by VS Code alone (CL-23).

rename: a block id.difference: VS Code searches .smd, .md and .markdown files for references (language.ts workspaceDocuments), the language server .smd files only (workspace.ts collect), so the link in notes.md is found by VS Code alone (CL-23). So VS Code also rewrites the link there.

rename: a heading.difference: VS Code searches .smd, .md and .markdown files for references (language.ts workspaceDocuments), the language server .smd files only (workspace.ts collect), so the link in notes.md is found by VS Code alone (CL-23). So VS Code also rewrites the link there.

triggerCharacters.difference: VS Code also triggers completion on a space (language.ts registers CompletionProvider with " "), which the language server does not advertise (lsp.ts TRIGGER_CHARACTERS) (CL-23). The footnote provider's "^" is registered apart in VS Code.
